subtopics.title: national facts
subtopics.teaching: National facts cover verified information about a country's geography, government, symbols, history and institutions.
subtopics.worked_example: India's Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, while its Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
subtopics.pitfall: Adoption and commencement are distinct dates and should not be conflated.
subtopics.mastery: Recall national facts precisely and distinguish closely related dates or institutions.

subtopics.title: world geography
subtopics.teaching: World geography includes continents, oceans, countries, physical features, climates and human settlement patterns.
subtopics.worked_example: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean, while Asia is the largest continent by area under common geographic classifications.
subtopics.pitfall: Largest and deepest, or continent and country, are different categories of comparison.
subtopics.mastery: Compare geographic entities using the property named in the question.

subtopics.title: capitals
subtopics.teaching: A capital is a designated political or administrative centre and is not always the largest or best-known city.
subtopics.worked_example: Canberra is Australia's capital, while Sydney is its largest city by population.
subtopics.pitfall: Familiarity with a city does not prove that it is the capital.
subtopics.mastery: Recall country-capital pairs and distinguish capitals from major cities.

subtopics.title: landmarks
subtopics.teaching: Landmarks may be natural, architectural, historical or cultural and are often identified through location and distinctive features.
subtopics.worked_example: The Eiffel Tower is a landmark of Paris, while the Taj Mahal is in Agra, India.
subtopics.pitfall: A landmark's country can be confused with its city when several facts are remembered together.
subtopics.mastery: Connect major landmarks with correct locations and broad significance.

subtopics.title: international organizations
subtopics.teaching: International organizations coordinate cooperation in areas such as health, peace, finance, development and culture.
subtopics.worked_example: The WHO focuses on international public health, while UNESCO works in areas including education, science and culture.
subtopics.pitfall: Organizations may cooperate on the same issue but have different mandates.
subtopics.mastery: Match major organizations with their principal functions.

subtopics.title: ancient civilizations
subtopics.teaching: Ancient civilizations can be identified through archaeological evidence, writing systems, cities, technology, governance and cultural practices.
subtopics.worked_example: The Indus Valley Civilization is associated with planned cities and sophisticated drainage systems.
subtopics.pitfall: A single artifact is rarely enough to define an entire civilization.
subtopics.mastery: Connect major civilizations with distinctive evidence and broad chronology.

subtopics.title: Indian history
subtopics.teaching: Indian history includes ancient, medieval and modern periods with many regional and political traditions.
subtopics.worked_example: The Mauryan Empire, Mughal Empire and Indian independence movement belong to different historical periods and political contexts.
subtopics.pitfall: Chronology prevents mixing people and events from unrelated periods.
subtopics.mastery: Place major Indian events and figures in broad chronological order.

subtopics.title: world history
subtopics.teaching: World history includes political, economic, scientific and social transformations across regions and centuries.
subtopics.worked_example: The Industrial Revolution changed production and urbanization, while the World Wars reshaped twentieth-century international relations.
subtopics.pitfall: A historical event's causes and consequences should be separated from later interpretations.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major world events and their broad historical significance.

subtopics.title: heritage
subtopics.teaching: Heritage includes tangible places and objects as well as cultural traditions passed between generations.
subtopics.worked_example: Ajanta and Ellora contain important rock-cut heritage associated with multiple religious and artistic traditions.
subtopics.pitfall: A heritage site's importance may involve several periods rather than one event.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major heritage examples and their cultural or historical context.

subtopics.title: historical personalities
subtopics.teaching: Historical personalities are associated with documented achievements, leadership, discoveries or cultural contributions.
subtopics.worked_example: Mahatma Gandhi is associated with India's independence movement and non-violent mass political action.
subtopics.pitfall: A quotation circulating online is not reliable evidence of authorship.
subtopics.mastery: Match personalities with verified contributions and historical contexts.

subtopics.title: life science
subtopics.teaching: Life science studies organisms, cells, heredity, body systems, ecosystems and biological processes.
subtopics.worked_example: Plants use photosynthesis to convert light energy into chemical energy, while animals obtain energy through food.
subtopics.pitfall: Photosynthesis and respiration are related but are not the same process.
subtopics.mastery: Distinguish major biological processes and apply them to familiar examples.

subtopics.title: physical science
subtopics.teaching: Physical science includes concepts from physics and chemistry such as matter, forces, energy, motion and reactions.
subtopics.worked_example: Speed can be calculated as distance divided by time, while mass and weight represent different physical quantities.
subtopics.pitfall: A formula should be used only when its variables match the quantity being asked.
subtopics.mastery: Apply basic physical and chemical concepts to everyday situations.

subtopics.title: Earth science
subtopics.teaching: Earth science examines rocks, minerals, atmosphere, water, weather, climate and geological processes.
subtopics.worked_example: The water cycle includes evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration and runoff.
subtopics.pitfall: Weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions while climate concerns long-term patterns.
subtopics.mastery: Connect Earth processes with observable environmental phenomena.

subtopics.title: space
subtopics.teaching: Space science studies planets, moons, stars, galaxies and the interactions among them.
subtopics.worked_example: Earth orbits the Sun and the Moon orbits Earth; the Sun is a star.
subtopics.pitfall: A galaxy is a much larger system than a planetary system.
subtopics.mastery: Classify major space objects and explain basic Earth-Sun-Moon relationships.

subtopics.title: environment
subtopics.teaching: Environmental science examines interactions among organisms, resources, pollution, climate and human activity.
subtopics.worked_example: Reducing waste and protecting habitats can help lower environmental pressure and conserve resources.
subtopics.pitfall: Recycling alone does not remove the environmental cost of producing and transporting materials.
subtopics.mastery: Identify environmental problems and evaluate practical conservation responses.

subtopics.title: computing
subtopics.teaching: Computing systems process information using hardware, software, memory, storage and networks.
subtopics.worked_example: RAM holds data for active work while persistent storage retains files when power is removed.
subtopics.pitfall: Storage capacity and processing speed are different properties.
subtopics.mastery: Identify core computing concepts and distinguish hardware roles.

subtopics.title: internet
subtopics.teaching: The internet connects networks worldwide, while web browsers and search engines are tools used to access and locate online information.
subtopics.worked_example: A browser retrieves a webpage, while a search engine helps locate relevant indexed pages.
subtopics.pitfall: The internet, web and search engine are related but not synonymous.
subtopics.mastery: Distinguish major internet concepts and tools.

subtopics.title: AI
subtopics.teaching: Artificial intelligence includes systems designed to perform tasks involving prediction, recognition, language or decision-making.
subtopics.worked_example: A generative AI system can produce text or images, but fluent output can still contain errors.
subtopics.pitfall: AI output should be checked rather than treated as automatically factual.
subtopics.mastery: Identify common AI uses and basic limitations.

subtopics.title: inventions
subtopics.teaching: Inventions apply ideas to solve practical problems and often build on earlier knowledge or technologies.
subtopics.worked_example: The telephone, printing press and semiconductor technologies each changed how people communicated or processed information.
subtopics.pitfall: Technological development is often cumulative rather than the work of one isolated moment.
subtopics.mastery: Connect major inventions with their broad purpose and impact.

subtopics.title: digital society
subtopics.teaching: Digital society concerns how technology affects communication, education, work, privacy, security and participation.
subtopics.worked_example: Digital platforms can increase access to information while also creating risks such as misinformation and privacy loss.
subtopics.pitfall: Technology's benefits do not remove the need for responsible use.
subtopics.mastery: Evaluate common social effects of digital technology.

subtopics.title: Indian literature
subtopics.teaching: Indian literature includes classical, medieval and modern works in many languages and traditions.
subtopics.worked_example: The Ramayana and Mahabharata have influenced literature and culture across many Indian languages and regions.
subtopics.pitfall: A major work may exist in multiple versions and adaptations.
subtopics.mastery: Connect major Indian works with their broad literary and cultural traditions.

subtopics.title: world literature
subtopics.teaching: World literature includes works from diverse languages, periods and cultures that have influenced global literary traditions.
subtopics.worked_example: Shakespeare's plays belong to the English Renaissance tradition, while Homer's epics belong to ancient Greek literary tradition.
subtopics.pitfall: Literary influence and original language are separate facts.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major world works, authors and broad literary contexts.

subtopics.title: arts
subtopics.teaching: Arts include visual and performing traditions such as painting, sculpture, theatre, dance and crafts.
subtopics.worked_example: Indian classical dance traditions such as Bharatanatyam and Kathak have distinct historical and performance conventions.
subtopics.pitfall: A folk tradition and a classical tradition should not be treated as identical categories.
subtopics.mastery: Recognize major art forms and associate them with appropriate traditions.

subtopics.title: music
subtopics.teaching: Music knowledge includes composers, performers, instruments, genres, traditions and characteristic forms.
subtopics.worked_example: The sitar is strongly associated with North Indian classical music traditions, while the veena has important South Indian classical traditions.
subtopics.pitfall: An instrument's presence in one tradition does not make it exclusive to that tradition.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major instruments, musicians and broad musical traditions.

subtopics.title: languages
subtopics.teaching: Languages belong to different families and have distinct scripts, histories and geographic distributions.
subtopics.worked_example: Tamil is a major Dravidian language with a long literary tradition, while Hindi belongs to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European family.
subtopics.pitfall: Language, script and official status are different concepts.
subtopics.mastery: Distinguish language families, scripts and official-language arrangements.
